You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

The installed workspace skills are stale (horizon, horizon-inbox, project-git, task-status). Do not overwrite deliberate local edits automatically, but do not ignore the drift. Until it is reconciled: use the `lean-check` LSP loop before and after Lean edits; spawn and wait for a bounded native subagent on multi-file/multi-proof work; and dispatch `janitor` (`ground` fallback) for inbox/roadmap/task health warnings and before terminal completion.

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: ajcr-divrep
Title: divRep and the datum tail: Div^g-lite representability through to the Pic^0 datum
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
References: roadmap=AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.datum-tail,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-g,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddq; inbox=I-0492,I-0494,I-0495

CLOSE THE divRep MOUNTAIN AND THE DATUM TAIL — the critical path to Challenge.lean:99. Roadmap AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep, its U2 gate, .datum-tail, and the assembly nodes dat-g / dat-glue / dat-j. READ informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md SECTION 7 FIRST: four rows of the section-1 table have MOVED, and section 7 carries the per-link evidence. Do not trust any MISSING claim in this project without checking the ledger for files added by an integrate commit — that is exactly how the round-4 framing went stale.

FIVE DELIVERABLES.

 (1) U2, THE LAST GATE (leaf ...divrep.u2, currently blocked and re-scoped TWICE). The DDR9-U epsilon-identity at the universal point: at the universal point the pair-chart tautological data must satisfy the epsilon identity. informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md section 3.1 is the specification. The second rescope CORRECTS a stale blocker this lane had been quoting — read the node before believing it is blocked, and if the blocker really is stale, say so and proceed.

 (2) divRep PROPER: package the affine classify/inverse laws, the DivFamZar and S6b interfaces, divRepAff, and the global RepresentableBy endpoint. What remains of L11 per section 7.1 is the general-test CLASSIFIER and the two inverse laws — the forward half is landed (DivRepAffinePullback.pullGlobal, Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean:102, with pullGlobal_comp at :132). L9 is rooted and kernel-checked; the two finiteness certificates of L3/L4 are no longer obligations (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom :154, quasiCompact_gluedHom :164 derive them).

 (3) THE DATUM TAIL: universal family, then feed DAT-B/C/Q, finite-stage descent, gluing, and the final Pic^0 RepresentableBy datum.

 (4) DAT-G AND DAT-GLUE: finite-Galois/Speiser descent of the PicRepDatum from a finite separable stage to the challenge field, and the 01JJ RepresentableBy assembly over k-prime (slice trick DAT-6). The 01JJ slice assembly is mechanically prepared at the separably closed stage; the remaining DAT-G0 work is filtered-colimit compatibility of pic0 plus descent of the representing datum.

 (5) DAT-J: JacobianData assembly — DJ-0 compact-image qc is landed; DJ-1 Abel-image qc and DJ-2 JacobianData packaging remain. Note JacobianData now has TWO producers (ofRepresentableBy :71 and ofCharts, Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:182, sorry-free and kernel-checked), which is more than the older docs say.

ONE SCARE ALREADY CLOSED, do not re-open it: the GeometricallyReduced hypothesis at Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:79 is REDUNDANT, not a gap — Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean:130/:140 supply it as instances and that module is in the import closure (machine-checked record at Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:210).

FALLBACK, if divRep genuinely stalls: leaf ...ddr.flattening-fallback (universal flattening strata or the affine Hilbert algebra chart) had its REJECTION REOPENED — the recorded rejection rationale was checked and is factually wrong, and it predates the route change that created the obligation. It is a legitimate option, not a dead end.

CONCURRENCY IS BINDING. Four AJCR teams at once. Follow informal/protocol-concurrent-lanes.md exactly: private-index compare-and-swap ledger commits (NEVER a bare git commit — it has silently reverted other lanes work three times), and the mkdir lake mutex at /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock (a DIRECTORY lock; never flock it).

COORDINATION. You depend on ajcr-cert-r2 for the widened DivFamZar shape — get the frozen shape from them on the AJCR conversation thread before building the classifier, and do not fork your own variant. ajcr-charts consumes your divRep endpoint; publish its signature early. ajcr-w5-av is downstream of the DD shape freeze. Never edit files outside Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild.

This is a headless, one-shot session: work the task's REAL objective as far
as you genuinely can, committing progress as you go, then finish with the
brief final report the skill specifies.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status current with `--status` and its strategy prose current with
60	  `--summary` / `--summary-file` (there is no `--strategy` flag). It doubles as
61	  the **project board**:
62	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
63	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
64	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
65	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
66	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
67	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
68	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
69	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
70	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
71	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
72	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
73	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
74	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
75	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
76	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
77	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
78	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
79	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
80	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
81	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
82	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
83	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
84	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
85	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
86	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
87	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
88	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
89	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
90	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
91	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
92	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
93	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
94	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
95	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
96	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
97	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
98	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
99	
100	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
101	
102	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
103	
104	| Variable | Meaning |
105	|---|---|
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
112	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
113	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
114	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
115	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
116	
117	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
118	
119	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
120	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
121	
122	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
123	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
124	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
125	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
126	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
127	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
128	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
129	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
130	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
131	
132	## One-shot discipline (important)
133	
134	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
135	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
136	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
137	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
138	
139	## Pick the highest-value work
140	
141	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
142	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
143	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
144	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
145	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
146	
147	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
148	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
149	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
150	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
151	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
152	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
153	(it returns to the queue).
154	
155	## Fresh-context checkpoints
156	
157	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
158	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
159	checkpoints:
160	
161	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
162	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
163	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
164	  clean/build result.
165	
166	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
167	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
168	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
169	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
170	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
171	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
172	terminal `done` claim.
173	
174	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
175	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
176	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
177	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
178	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
179	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
180	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
181	
182	## Warnings are work
183	
184	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
185	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
186	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
187	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
188	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
189	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
190	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
191	why.
192	
193	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
194	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
195	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
196	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
197	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
198	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
199	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
200	
201	## Do the work (Lean)
202	
203	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
204	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
205	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
206	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
207	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
208	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
209	configured final build covers the same files.
210	
211	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
212	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
213	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
214	mathlib — query it:
215	
216	| You want | Use | Not |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
219	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
220	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
221	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
222	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
223	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
224	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
225	
226	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
227	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
228	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
229	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
230	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
231	back to grep.
232	
233	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
234	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
235	
236	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
237	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
238	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
239	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
240	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
241	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
242	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
243	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
244	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
245	
246	## Read the other projects
247	
248	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
249	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
250	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
251	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
252	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
253	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
254	
255	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
256	
257	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
258	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
259	needs no permission.
260	
261	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
262	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
263	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
264	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
265	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
266	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
267	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
268	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
269	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
270	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
271	
272	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
273	
274	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
275	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
276	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
277	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
278	
279	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
280	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
281	
282	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status (`--status`) and strategy prose
283	  (`--summary`), not a re-narration of the diff.
284	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
285	  as **memory**.
286	
287	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
288	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
289	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
290	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
291	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
292	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
293	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
294	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
295	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
296	
297	## Resuming after an interruption
298	
299	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
300	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
301	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
302	
303	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
304	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
305	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
306	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
307	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
308	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
309	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
310	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
311	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
312	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
313	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
314	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
315	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
316	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
317	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
318	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
319	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
320	
321	## Final report (your last message)
322	
323	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
324	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
325	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,

218	### 7.3 §2's "one open experiment" was already answered, by this file's own sibling
219	
220	§2 closes with *"At `g ≥ 2` no witness has ever been exhibited… It is not acceptable to keep
221	planning without knowing which."* That question was settled in the **same round**:
222	`informal/spec-dd-r.md` **ADDENDUM 4** (commit `d7e8348ce`) is titled *"the on-stratum witness
223	EXISTS"*, and roadmap leaf `…ddr.certificate.field-size` is `done` carrying the sharp theorem.
224	
225	**The conclusion stands on ADDENDUM 4, not on what follows.** A ground review corrected the
226	first draft of this subsection, which claimed the argument below "agrees with" ADDENDUM 4 and holds
227	"over any field". It does neither. ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 uses the universal divisor over `Sym^g C`,
228	base-changes to an extension and pads by `(g−1)Q₀`, and states at `spec-dd-r.md:826` that no
229	rational-point hypothesis is used anywhere. What follows is a **different, cheaper witness** — a
230	pencil rather than `Sym^g` — with a side condition ADDENDUM 4 does not need:
231	
232	> For any `g ≥ 2`, take a pencil of degree `g` on `C` one of whose members is a divisor
233	> `E ≥ s₀ + s_∞` with `π(s₀) = 0`, `π(s_∞) = ∞`. Such an `E` exists: `ℓ(E) = 1 + ℓ(K − E)`, so any
234	> `E` with `s₀ + s_∞ ≤ E ≤ K'` for a canonical `K' ≥ s₀ + s_∞` has `ℓ(E) ≥ 2`; and such a `K'`
235	> exists because `ℓ(K − s₀ − s_∞) ≥ g − 2 ≥ 1` for `g ≥ 3`, and for `g = 2` exactly when `s_∞` is
236	> the hyperelliptic conjugate of `s₀` (which one is free to arrange, since `π` is a choice: a
237	> function with a zero at `s₀` and a pole at `s_∞` is a finite map sending them to `0` and `∞`).
238	> The support of the total family is an open subscheme of the irreducible `C`, hence irreducible,
239	> hence **connected after every Zariski shrink of the base** — which is exactly why the shrink
240	> evasion that kills the `g = 1` case does not apply here.
241	
242	**The side condition, and it is not cosmetic.** Writing `s₀ + s_∞` and computing
243	`ℓ(K − s₀ − s_∞) ≥ g − 2` treats `s₀, s_∞` as *degree-1* points. Over a non-closed field the
244	minimal closed points `q₀ ∈ π⁻¹(0)`, `q₁ ∈ π⁻¹(∞)` have residue degrees `e₀, e₁`, and an effective
245	`E ≥ q₀ + q₁` of degree `g` exists only if **`e₀ + e₁ ≤ g`**. Over `𝔽₂` with `g = 2` and
246	`e₀ = e₁ = 2` this witness does not exist — which is exactly the regime ADDENDUM 4 §4.4's
247	"only if" direction isolates. Secondly, the `g = 2` case above needs `π` chosen so that `s_∞` is
248	the hyperelliptic conjugate of `s₀`, whereas ADDENDUM 4 holds for any finite dominant `π`.
249	
250	So: **the fixed-pair certificate route is dead on the campaign's own stratum** — on ADDENDUM 4's
251	authority, for every field; and the pencil above is a cheaper witness for the sub-case
252	`e₀ + e₁ ≤ g`. Do not re-run this experiment. Do not formalise either witness — ADDENDUM 4 §4.5
253	explains why (it needs `Sym^g C` / `Hilb^g`, and this tree constructs no curve other than `P¹`).
254

307	## 7.6 The gate is L8, not U2 — and that is the round's main finding
308	
309	Inbox **I-0365**. The framing "the divrep tail is independent of the certificate; the certificate
310	gates U2" is false, but not in the direction the tree assumed.
311	
312	`DivFamZar` is **by definition** a quotient of *locally certified* families
313	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:224` the setoid, `:235` the def, `:71` `IsLocallyCertified` — note it
314	localises on the base only). So certificates are **free on the consuming side**:
315	`DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover` (`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean:433`) is a landed theorem,
316	unfolded by every classifier keystone (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:128/:176/:230`,
317	`DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean:361/:363`), and `IsDivRepClassify` (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:90`)
318	quantifies over certified families as a *hypothesis*, so their scarcity makes it easier, not harder.
319	
320	The bite is on the other side. The no-go (`DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:123` — clause (c1) *is*
321	leak-freeness — and `:131`) says `DivFamZar` is blind to connected divisors meeting both pinned
322	fibres. So `divFunctor C π g` is a **proper subfunctor** of degree-`g` relative divisors.
323	Representing it is not the problem; the L9–L13 tail does that honestly. The problem is that a
324	too-small divisor functor **cannot cover Pic⁰**: the Abel map out of it is not Zariski-locally
325	surjective, because the classes whose only witnesses are the invisible divisors are never hit.
326	
327	One nuance that sharpens where to look: the no-go's hypothesis is `IsPreconnected d.supportLocus`,
328	and **over a field it is vacuous** — the support of a divisor is a finite set of closed points, so
329	preconnected forces a single point, which cannot meet two disjoint fibres. The blindness is a
330	purely *relative* phenomenon: a family over a positive-dimensional base whose total support is a
331	connected horizontal curve sweeping from `π⁻¹(0)` to `π⁻¹(∞)` is invisible, and base shrinking does
332	not help because every neighbourhood of the crossing contains points on both sides. So
333	Riemann–Roch-level, fibrewise coverage is untouched — but local surjectivity of a *presheaf* map is
334	tested on arbitrary scheme tests, which is exactly the relative direction.
335	
336	**Consequences.** (i) Stop calling U2 or the affine package "the gate": they are tail work and are
337	nearly finished. (ii) Do not attack L8 against `divFunctor` as it stands — it is arguably false,
338	not merely hard. (iii) Judge R1 and R2 by whether they widen `DivFamZar` enough for L8, not by
339	whether they make a certificate easier to prove. A third widening is worth costing beside them:
340	replace `IsLocallyCertified` outright by the standard relative effective Cartier divisor (finite
341	locally free of rank `g` over the base), which carries no chart-adaptation artifact at all.
342

487	## 7.9 ROUND-0071 s0006 AMENDMENT: U2 is an equation, and DAT-J's "step 3" was two steps
488	
489	*Run 0071 session 0006, task `ajcr-divrep`, 2026-07-28. All Lean below is sorry-free, kernel-checked
490	(`lake env lean` exit 0 per file), rooted, in a green root build at **9176 jobs**, and axiom-probed
491	at `propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound` **with a control (`Jacobian`) that still reports
492	`sorryAx`**, so the readings mean something.*
493	
494	### 7.9.1 U2 carries no quantifier: it is an equation between two landed morphisms
495	
496	§7.8 reduced the tail to one hypothesis, `IsChartClause`, and read it as the ε-identity — a
497	*submodule* identity, quantified inside `IsDivRepClassify` over all tower tests and all framings.
498	That quantifier is not there. `Picard/DivRepChartRange.lean`:
499	
500	> `isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq` :
501	> `IsDivRepClassify F₀ v ↔ (divRepClassifyZar … F₀).left = v`
502	
503	**Why, and this is the whole content.** `divRepClassifyZar` is **total** — defined for every
504	locally certified class over every affine test, with no hypotheses beyond the ambient ones — and
505	`isDivRepClassify_unique` makes it the *unique* morphism satisfying the clause. So the clause is
506	not a property one verifies of `v`; it says `v` **is** the classifier. Forward is uniqueness,
507	backward is a rewrite. The statement names no chart family and no universal point, so it serves
508	anyone holding an `IsDivRepClassify` obligation.
509	
510	Hence, and **stated as an `iff` on purpose** (inbox `I-0571`: a restatement is a reduction only
511	when the converse is proved — both directions are):
512	
513	> `DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq` :
514	> `IsChartClause U ↔ ∀ i j, (divRepClassifyZar … (U i j)).left = ChartMap i j`
515	
516	So **U2 is a per-chart equation between two morphisms `Spec R_Z(i,j) ⟶ DivScheme g` that both
517	already exist as landed terms.** Reading off the existential:
518	
519	> `divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` :
520	> `(∀ i j, ∃ F, (divRepClassifyZar … F).left = ChartMap i j) → (divFunctor C π g).RepresentableBy DivOver`
521	
522	Since `divRepClassifyZar` is injective on classes (`eq_of_isDivRepClassify`), representability of
523	`divFunctor` is *equivalent* to surjectivity of the classifier at every affine test; what is new is
524	that **surjectivity at the chart rings alone suffices**. The remaining debt is a *preimage under a
525	landed map* at `glueData`-many points.
526	
527	**No gate cleared.** Nothing produces a term of `DivFamZar C (DivCarveChartRing … i j) π g`; U2 is
528	unproved, and the endpoint still carries `hO`, `hχ` and the ambient curve instances, so "one
529	equation" describes the debt and not representability for an arbitrary `C`.
530	
531	**But the G-4 quote should be re-measured, not re-quoted.** This row has already outlived one stale
532	blocker (the I-0234 `windowS` strengthening, which was `done`). Two facts say the same scrutiny is
533	owed to "U2 is gated on a *global* `IsCertified` over the chart ring":
534	
535	* `Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean` exists to remove exactly that. Its docstring states that
536	  **nothing downstream of `DivFamZar` asks for a certificate over `R` itself**, and
537	  `ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamZar_of_forall_away_certified` (`:132`) produces the class from
538	  **away-local** certificates. `Picard/DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean` goes further —
539	  `divFamZar_of_forall_prime_away_certified` (`:181`) needs a certificate only *after shrinking at
540	  each prime*, which is the shape the support tube actually produces.
541	* Inbox `I-0602` (cert-r2, machine-measured) gives the general trap: the chart-typing that
542	  `divRepClassifyZar`'s signature *appears* to require is not what its body consumes — `divFamEps`
543	  reads only the `eqns` field, through `divisorWindow`, and the framing clause mentions no cover, no
544	  piece and no chart typing.
545	
546	Neither fact proves the gate is stale and this amendment does not claim it. It says: **measure it in
547	Lean before spending another session treating it as a wall.**
548	
549	### 7.9.2 DAT-J: §7.8's closing paragraph undercounted, and the assembly was never written
550	
551	§7.8 ends "*What remains of DAT-J is step 3 alone: surjectivity of the Abel map on points*". Step 3
552	was **two** statements, and one of them was not mathematics about the Jacobian at all.
553	
554	* **The bridge** (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean`). §2.3's argument (the `fiberTwist` shift plus
555	  `exists_effective_of_picClass`) delivers, for a point `y`, a **morphism** `Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g`.
556	  The qc field consumes `Function.Surjective abel.base`. **Nothing converted one into the other.**
557	  `surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` does: `κ(y)` is a field hence `Spec κ(y)` is
558	  nonempty, and mathlib's `range_fromSpecResidueField` pins the range to `{y}`. Pure scheme
559	  topology — no curve, no Picard functor, no divisor scheme — hence reusable. With DJ-0 it gives
560	  `quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme`, `JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` and
561	  `JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts` (the infinite-atlas producer §7.5 asks for).
562	* **The DAT-G handoff** (`Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean`). w4-datj §1.1 pins DJ-IN =
563	  `PicRepDatum k k C` and asserts the packaging is free because the `rep` field types are
564	  definitionally equal. **The packaging had never been written**, and the tell is sharp:
565	  `PicRepDatum` occurred in *no other Lean file in the tree*, its defeq recorded as an `example`
566	  that nothing consumed. `PicRepDatum.toJacobianData` is the first declaration to use it, so the
567	  worksheet's assertion is now a machine fact rather than an assertion.
568	
569	**What DAT-J now owes is visible in one signature and nowhere else** —
570	`PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` takes exactly a `PicRepDatum k k C` (DAT-G/DAT-G0,
571	divRep-gated) and a per-point lift. Both remain open; the lift stays binding-Challenge-free per §0.5
572	(`exists_effective_of_picClass` / `riemann_inequality`, **never** `riemann_inequality_curve`).
573	
574	### 7.9.3 §7.6 stands
575	
576	L8 — local surjectivity of the Abel map out of a too-small divisor functor — remains the campaign's
577	real gate and is arguably false as stated. Nothing above bears on it. The tail becoming an equation
578	is not progress toward L8, and should not be read as any.

12	byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:
13	
14	```bash
15	cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
16	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
17	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
18	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
19	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
20	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
21	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
22	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
23	  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>
24	
25	Archon-Commit: agent
26	Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
27	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
28	unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
29	```
30	
31	If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
32	ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
33	A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.
34	
35	### 1a. THE RECIPE ABOVE HAS A RACE — read HEAD ONCE, not twice (2026-07-28, run 0072)
36	
37	**As written, the recipe reads `HEAD` twice**: once in `read-tree HEAD`, and again several lines
38	later in `PARENT=$(… rev-parse HEAD)`. If another lane's CAS lands **between those two reads**,
39	your tree is built from the *old* snapshot while your parent is the *new* commit — and
40	`update-ref` **succeeds**, because it only checks that the ref has not moved since `rev-parse`.
41	It never checks that the tree was built from that ref. You publish a stale tree, silently
42	reverting everything that landed in the window.
43	
44	**Measured once, and the measurement is narrow — do not over-read it.** `e964967e8` has parent
45	`a1ef4d59c` and, diffed against *that parent*, deletes 95 lines of
46	`informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md`, 52 of `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` and 19 of
47	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean` — exactly the restore `a1ef4d59c` had just performed, undone.
48	Its `read-tree` ran before `a1ef4d59c` landed; its parent was captured after. It staged explicit
49	paths and the pathspec *was* honoured: **the sweep came from the TREE BASE, not the pathspec**,
50	which is why "stage explicit files" is not a defence and why the symptom is indistinguishable
51	from §1b's shared-index staleness.
52	
53	**Two other lanes audited their own CAS commits the same day (fifteen commits between them,
54	recipe verbatim) and found zero reverts.** That is consistent with this: the race only fires when
55	another lane's CAS lands inside your particular window, so clean commits are the expected
56	outcome, not evidence of absence. The discriminating question is not "did my commits look clean"
57	but "was my `read-tree` separated from my `rev-parse` by somebody else's commit". Treat §1a as
58	cheap insurance, not as a diagnosis of every mystery revert — and check §1b too.
59	
60	**The fix is one line — capture the parent BEFORE the tree, and read-tree that sha:**
61	
62	```bash
63	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)     # ONCE, up front
64	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
65	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree $PARENT      # not "HEAD"
66	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
67	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
68	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD … commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "…")
69	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # now genuinely atomic
70	```
71	
72	Then a mid-recipe CAS by another lane makes `update-ref` **fail**, you re-read and retry, and the
73	protocol behaves as it was meant to. The verification step ("must touch only your paths") is what
74	catches it after the fact — run it every time, and read the file list, not just the count.
75	
76	### 1b. The CAS recipe leaves the SHARED index permanently stale — this is by design, and it is armed
77	
78	Added 2026-07-27 (run 0048 r5) after this failed a **third** time (`I-0366`: the shared index
79	was pinned to a pre-round-5 snapshot and a bare `git commit` would have deleted
80	`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).
81	
82	The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
83	publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
84	The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
85	describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
86	including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
87	the shared index drifts behind.
88	
89	Consequences, all three binding:
90	
91	1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
92	   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
93	2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
94	   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
95	   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
96	   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
97	3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
98	   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
99	   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).
100	
101	Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
102	the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.
103	
104	## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there
105	
106	`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
107	directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
108	that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
109	path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
110	15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:
111	
112	```bash
113	LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
114	while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
115	  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
116	  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
117	  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
118	  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
119	    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
120	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
121	      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
122	    fi
123	    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
124	    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
125	       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
126	      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
127	    fi
128	  fi
129	  sleep 10
130	done
131	echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
132	# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
133	```
134	
135	Two stale shapes, both now handled above (do NOT just `sleep` forever on either):
136	- A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir makes directories) — reap immediately.
137	- An orphaned DIRECTORY from a build that crashed before `rm -rf` (the 2026-07-19 C4 incident,
138	  I-0257): the OLD acquire loop only checked for a file, so it spun forever on this. Writing
139	  `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` on acquire lets the next lane prove the holder is dead (`kill -0`) and reap
140	  safely; the no-pidfile branch (a holder from before this fix) falls back to "no live build + >15min".
141	  Never reap a directory whose pidfile names a LIVE pid — that is a real build in progress.
142	
143	## 3. /tmp quota with >3 lanes
144	
145	uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide
146	(~19:00–19:20). With more than ~3 concurrent lanes, keep scratch artifacts small, clean up
147	build temp dirs, and if Bash starts failing with quota errors, stop and report rather than
148	retry-looping.
149	
150	## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)
151	
152	`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
153	sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
154	in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
155	YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
156	`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
157	other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
158	HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
159	only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
160	root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.
161	
162	### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)
163	
164	The check above works. The failure mode is **misreading** it, and it happened again on
165	2026-07-28: the diff printed a `-import`/`+import` pair from a sibling lane's *uncommitted*
166	worktree edit, the committing lane read it as background noise, and the commit published the
167	sibling's replacement — dropping `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` from the import closure.
168	The file stayed in HEAD and still compiled, but was reachable from nothing: **un-rooted**,
169	i.e. I-0153 again, from a lane that had run the I-0153 check.
170	
171	So state the rule in a form that needs no judgement:
172	
173	> **A `-import` line in that diff is never yours.** The only clean result is `+import <your
174	> file>` and nothing else. Any minus line means you are about to delete another lane's root
175	> entry — stop and explain it before committing. An unexplained `+import` you did not write
176	> is the same signal: a sibling's uncommitted edit is in your worktree copy, and a minus line
177	> usually accompanies it.
178	
179	This is strictly stronger than "commit only your own lines", because you can intend that and
180	still sweep — staging the whole file is what publishes their edit, and the diff is your only
181	warning.
182	
183	**Repair additively, never by reverting.** Restore the dropped import while **keeping** the
184	other lane's new one, then verify with a full root build (the 2026-07-28 repair: 9139 jobs,
185	exit 0, with the un-rooted file rebuilt). Reverting to your own earlier root blob discards
186	their work and turns one incident into two.
187	
188	## 5. The AJCR mutex is for AJCR lake invocations only
189	
190	No cross-workspace use (an OpenGA-Horizon agent squatted it ~25 min for its own
191	`lake cache get`, silently serializing AJCR lanes against unrelated work). Other
192	workspaces must use their own lock paths.
193	
194	### 5a. Read it as per-PROJECT, not per-workspace (2026-07-28, run 0072)
195	
196	The rule above says "cross-workspace", and that wording has a hole: **AJC and AJCR are two
197	projects in the SAME workspace.** Observed live on 2026-07-28 — the AJCR mutex was held for
198	over ten minutes while the only live `lake build` belonged to an `ajc-*` lane building
199	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, the sibling project. Same failure as the
200	OpenGA incident, not covered by the rule as written.
201	
202	The lock path is `ajcr-locks`, so read the rule as: **only lanes building
203	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` may take it.** AJC lanes need their own path
204	(`/tmp/claude-1001/ajc-locks/lake.lock`). Note the AJC task prompts do not mention a mutex
205	at all, which is very likely why an AJC lane reached for this one.
206	
207	### 5b. Write the pidfile — the no-pidfile fallback cannot distinguish squatter from orphan
208	
209	§2's acquire recipe writes `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` so a later lane can prove death via
210	`kill -0`. In the incident above the lock directory had **no pidfile**, so that branch could
211	not fire and the fallback ("no live `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` **and** dir >15 min old")
212	also could not fire — there *was* a live build, just not an AJCR one. Net effect: a
213	provably-non-AJCR holder is unreapable for 15 minutes.
214	
215	Two consequences for a blocked lane, both applied in that incident:
216	
217	* **Do not reap a directory whose holder you cannot prove dead**, even when you suspect a
218	  squatter. Reaping mid-build is worse than waiting.
219	* **Fall back to the narrowest check instead of blocking.** `lake env lean <file>` on the
220	  single changed file writes no shared build state and needs no lock; it is a faithful
221	  kernel check for that file. Record in the report that the mutex was unavailable and which
222	  check you substituted.

41	classifier is already a bijection onto its range everywhere, and the whole remaining debt

221	    (hrange : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),

13	The DD-R endgame consumes divisor families through `DivFamZar` (`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`),

17	certificate over `R` itself.**

20	`(D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g` over the chart ring `R_Z`, whose no-leak input
21	is exactly the hypothesis that is FALSE for arbitrary extracted pieces (I-0209: a piece
22	whose support trace leaks has a non-finite colength, and the localization repair breaks
23	finiteness over `R`).  The lane has been paying for a strictly stronger statement than
24	its consumer needs.
25	
26	This file lands the relaxation.  `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` says: to
27	certify a system *Zariski-locally* it suffices to produce, for each member of some
28	span-`⊤` family, a certified family over that localization which is divisor-equal to the
29	pulled system.  Then `ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_isCertified`
30	specializes it to a seed: if the seed's adaptation acquires a certificate **after
31	localizing at each member of a span-`⊤` family** — which is precisely what the support
32	tube produces (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`: piece isolation is available

37	produced from local data and that the seed's pulled system over an away localization is

46	  the seed form: away-local certificates give a locally certified seed system.

CROSS-PROJECT THREAD — AJC and AJCR are doing the same mathematics twice; this is where you stop that

Eight teams launched on 2026-07-28, four on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge and four on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild. The two projects overlap heavily and the workspace exists so the same lemma is not derived twice. This thread is for cross-project leads ONLY — per-project coordination goes on your own project thread.

THREE OVERLAPS ALREADY IDENTIFIED, with the evidence:

 1. THE ETALE-PLUS PICARD FUNCTOR. AJCR has it BUILT AND SORRY-FREE: Picard/PicEtAff.lean (394 lines), Picard/Pic0Functor.lean (182), Picard/RelPicCoverInjective.lean (89) — I re-verified zero sorries on 2026-07-28. AJC is about to need exactly this, because the human decision of today (protection I-0491) makes the etale-sheafified functor its representability target. ajc-etale-pic: read those three files BEFORE writing anything, then post here what you are porting, importing, or re-deriving and why. AJCR teams: correct them if they are about to reinvent something you have.

 2. dim T_0(Pic^0) = g, THE TANGENT/H1 COMPARISON. Being worked from BOTH sides simultaneously: ajc-pic0av on Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean (tangentSpaceCotangentDual, finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_finrank_h1Cok) and ajcr-w5-av on the T1/T3/T4/T5 chain. AJCRs T4 carries a real risk (the etale-plus / Zariski kernel crossing at k[epsilon]) that AJC may not face in the same form, or may face worse — that comparison is worth a post on its own.

 3. THE RIEMANN-ROCH / CLUSTER-P SUBSTRATE. AJCR has a 63-file, 17.8k-line RiemannRoch/ directory that is largely sorry-free and is essentially the cluster-P substrate AJC lacks. A predecessor assessment judged that auditing it for portability decides where the next two months go, more than any single proof would. Nobody is tasked with that audit today — so if your work touches it, post what you learn about portability. Note the standing caveat: much of AJCs adelic RR work is conditional in the STATEMENT on a closed chi-ledger or a peel datum, so read scripts/axiom-frontier.lean sections 6b/6d before treating any of it as available.

/-! ## The campaign spellings (the DAT-D windows) -/

section Curve

open Scheme

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(divisorSections k B ⊤))
variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))

/-- **The chart atlas of `DivScheme g`** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.3): each
`Z(♦)`-chart `Spec R_Z` maps to `DivScheme g`, factoring the chart presentation through
`divSchemeι`.  The kill law is `divCarveIdeal_le_ker_of_tower` at the chart ring itself
(spelled `Ideal.mk_ker`). -/
noncomputable def divCarveChartToDivScheme
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
    Spec (CommRingCat.of (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j))
      ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ :=
  carveLocusToCarveScheme k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j

/-- **The defining triangle of the `DivScheme` chart atlas**: through the closed immersion
`divSchemeι`, the chart map of `Spec R_Z` is `Spec` of the quotient presentation
`divCarveChartMk` followed by the pair chart. -/
theorem divCarveChartToDivScheme_divSchemeι
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
    divCarveChartToDivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (divCarveChartMk k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j).toRingHom)
        ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j :=
  carveLocusToCarveScheme_carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j

/-- **The atlas factorization of `DivScheme g`** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.3,
the DDR-9.F1 keystone): every test morphism `v : overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver` factors,
over a finite spanning family of basic localizations of `S`, through some chart
`divCarveChartToDivScheme i j` along a `k`-algebra map
`ω : R_Z →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)` out of the `Z(♦)`-chart ring. -/
theorem divScheme_exists_chartFactor (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → S), Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ t : Fin m, ∃ (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
        (ω : DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)),
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ω.toRingHom)
            ≫ divCarveChartToDivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j
          = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S (Localization.Away (f t))))
            ≫ v.left :=
  carveScheme_exists_chartFactor k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) S v

end Curve

end AlgebraicGeometry
